gloss: to have no room; to have no time or money to spare

definitions.gloss: to have no room; to have no leeway; to be pressed for time, money, or capacity
definitions.explanation: Expresses a lack of spare time, money, mental capacity, or physical space. Often used to explain why one cannot take on additional tasks or obligations.

examples.japanese: {今|いま}は{余裕|よゆう}がない。
examples.english: I don't have any room right now.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しくて、{趣味|しゅみ}をする{余裕|よゆう}がない。
examples.english: I'm so busy with work that I have no time for hobbies.

examples.japanese: {今月|こんげつ}は{出費|しゅっぴ}が{多|おお}くて、{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}く{余裕|よゆう}がない。
examples.english: I've had so many expenses this month that I can't afford to travel.

notes:
USAGE:
{余裕|よゆう} means "margin," "leeway," or "room to spare." The expression {余裕|よゆう}がない indicates a complete lack of spare capacity in any dimension — time, money, energy, or emotional bandwidth. It is a very common and natural way to decline invitations or explain one's constraints.

The positive form {余裕|よゆう}がある means to have plenty of room or time to spare.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}の{余裕|よゆう}がない (to have no spare time)
- {金銭的|きんせんてき}な{余裕|よゆう}がない (to have no financial leeway)
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}がない (to have no emotional room)
- {気持|きも}ちの{余裕|よゆう}がない (to be mentally overwhelmed)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {暇|ひま}がない: to have no free time — more specific to time
- {手一杯|ていっぱい}: to have one's hands full — emphasizes being at capacity with tasks
